case_title: J. VEDHASINGH v. R.M. GOVINDAN & ORS.
statutory_provisions: NI Act s.138, IPC ss.120B, 406, 420 and 34
neutral_facts: The accused, who was working as a Civil Engineer in Saudi Arabia, returned to India in 2011 and purchased a site from the respondent. The respondents owned seven other house sites in total, which were mortgaged to a corporation. The accused entered into a profit-sharing agreement with the respondents and invested a sum of money. However, the respondents did not share the profits or provide any land. The accused was promised repayment and received a cheque for repayment, which was dishonored. The accused filed a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Prior to this, the accused had lodged a complaint under Section 156(3) CrPC, which was dismissed. The accused then filed a protest petition, which was allowed, leading to the registration of a case against the respondents for offences under Sections 120B, 406, 420, and 34 of the IPC. The respondents challenged the proceedings, arguing that the same facts were already being investigated under the NI Act, and the High Court quashed the proceedings, stating that the prosecution under the IPC would amount to abuse of process.
